glycogen phosphorylases are light dark regulated enzymes that are activated by phosphorylation and deactivated by reduction of the enzyme.

the regulation of the enzyme glycogen phosphorylases in a blue-green alga, Anabena cylindrica.

the elucidation of the molecular basis of the regulation of glycogen phosphorylation in the blue-green alga,  Anacystis  nidulans, and with the role of this enzyme in the mobilization process.

glycogen phosphorylases from different sources are regulated by different mechanisms and that the light-dark modulation is not a general phenomenon.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glycogen phosphorylases in the cyanobacterium Anacystis  nidulans are subject to regulation in response to changes in environmental factors.
the enzyme activity is modulated by the photosynthetic electron flow and the reducing power of the cell, which in turn are controlled by the light-dark regime.
